metadata.technology: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe (with MCU + radio)
metadata.technology_specification: Capacitive soil moisture sensor probe with integrated microcontroller unit (MCU) and wireless radio module
metadata.technology_reasoning: Capacitive soil moisture sensors are the most common type due to their corrosion resistance and reliability in soil moisture detection. Integration with an MCU and a wireless radio module is standard in modern sensor probes to enable on-site data processing and remote communication, widely adopted in smart agriculture as of 2024.

components.reasoning: This is the core sensing element that detects soil moisture via capacitance changes. It is universally present and procured or manufactured as a distinct module or PCB section.
The MCU processes sensor signals and manages data communication. It is a fundamental electronic component always present and often integrated on the sensor PCB.

components.component: Wireless Radio Module (e.g., LoRa, Zigbee, or BLE)
components.reasoning: Used for wireless data transmission to gateways or data loggers. Wireless communication is a defining feature of such smart probes and the radio module is typically a separate procurement unit or module.
The PCB hosts the sensor interface, MCU, radio module, and associated electronics. It is a separately manufactured assembly essential to the device.

components.component: Power Supply Module (e.g., battery or energy harvesting unit)
components.reasoning: Most probes require a reliable power source. Batteries or energy harvesting units (solar cells) are distinct components supplying power.
This structural component protects electronics from soil, moisture, and mechanical damage; typically procured separately as injection molded plastic or coated metal.
